summary: Of 24 key details Brendan Dassey stated or agreed to across three recorded sessions, investigators introduced 10 first, the suspect introduced 9 first, 4 were already public, and 1 may trace to an earlier unrecorded statement. Multiple details were adopted only after investigators mentioned them, including several adopted by agreeing to leading questions. Interrogation tactics included repeated “we already know” assertions (52 total), minimization, and demands for truth. Two sessions on February 27, 2006 (S1b, S1c) have no public transcript.
key_points: Investigators stated 10 of 24 key details before the suspect did; the suspect stated 9 first; 4 were public before any interview; 1 (bleach on jeans) may trace to an unrecorded evening session with Fassbender on Feb 27, 2006 (Decision and Order p. 7, citing ECF 19-19 at 10-11).

Five details were adopted by agreeing to investigator questions: license plates removed (p. wiegert, p. brendan), Avery raised hood (p. wiegert, p. brendan), vehicle key in bedroom (p. fassbender, p. brendan), bleach on jeans (p. wiegert, p. brendan), phone/camera/purse burned (p. fassbender, p. brendan).
Investigators mentioned the body-burned detail 21 times before the suspect adopted it (p. fassbender, p. brendan); the detail was also public as of Nov 16, 2005.
The tattoo detail was raised by investigators (p. fassbender) but never adopted by the suspect.
Across sessions, interrogators used “we already know” 52 times (S1: 6, S2: 36, S3: 10), minimization 30 times, and demands for truth 85 times.
Two February 27 sessions (Two Rivers PD and evening with Fassbender) have no public transcript; the bleach detail is documented only via a court order referencing an unproduced record.
limits: This audit traces only the sequence of detail appearance in the available transcripts; it cannot assess the truth or falsity of any detail.
It cannot evaluate the content or influence of the two unrecorded February 27 sessions (S1b, S1c).
It does not measure the voluntariness or reliability of the suspect’s statements, nor the effect of interrogation tactics on memory or suggestibility.
It does not determine whether suspect-first details originated from independent knowledge or from unrecorded contacts.
